result.summary: Root cause confirmed by direct code trace (no speculation): the @type manifest() in lib/letflow/modules/module.ex types both :permissions and :role_grants values as plain atom(), making it impossible for Dialyzer or the compiler to enforce the subset constraint between the two fields. The only current enforcement is Catalog.validate_granted_permissions_declared/1, which fires at test/runtime only. Dialyzer-only type refinement is infeasible for a relational cross-field constraint in Elixir's type system. The recommended fix is a defmanifest/1 macro in module.ex that validates the constraint at module compile time and raises CompileError if violated. The existing runtime validate/1 check and its test coverage are unchanged. No prior resolved match in the issue registry — ISS-0790 is the canonical first filing, pre-announced by decision record 0039.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design

handoff_context.constraint_to_enforce: Every atom in the values of manifest.role_grants must also appear in manifest.permissions — currently enforced only by Catalog.validate_granted_permissions_declared/1 at runtime/test time; must also be enforced at compile time via defmanifest/1 macro or equivalent mechanism.
handoff_context.do_not_change: Catalog.validate/1, validate_granted_permissions_declared/1, and all six validation rules — runtime behavior must remain unchanged per AC2.

root_cause.summary: The `Letflow.Modules.Module` behaviour's `@type manifest()` declaration types both `permissions` and `role_grants` values as plain `atom()` / `[atom()]`. Elixir's type system — and Dialyzer by extension — has no mechanism to express a relational / dependent constraint between two sibling fields of the same map type: specifically, that every atom appearing as a value in the `role_grants` map must also appear in the `permissions` list. This is structurally a subset constraint across two independent fields of the same struct/map, which is outside the expressible domain of Elixir's type system. As a result, a module author who writes `role_grants: %{SOME_ROLE: [:Undeclared]}` where `:Undeclared` is absent from `permissions` will receive no compile-time feedback whatsoever.
root_cause.where_the_gap_lives: lib/letflow/modules/module.ex — @type manifest() at the `required(:permissions)` and `required(:role_grants)` field declarations
root_cause.what_catches_it_today: Only `Letflow.Modules.Catalog.validate_granted_permissions_declared/1` (catalog.ex, the private validation helper) catches this, and only when `Catalog.validate/1` is explicitly called — which happens in CatalogTest (test/letflow/modules/catalog_test.exs, the 'rejects a role_grants value not in the module's own permissions' test case), not during compilation of the module itself.

findings: lib/letflow/modules/module.ex declares `@type manifest()` with `required(:permissions) => [atom()]` and `required(:role_grants) => %{atom() => [atom()]}`. Both fields accept any atoms — Dialyzer sees no relationship between them.

@callback manifest/0 returns `manifest()` — this means any module implementing the callback can return a manifest where role_grants contains atoms absent from permissions and the compiler will emit no warning or error.

lib/letflow/modules/catalog.ex's `validate_granted_permissions_declared/1` (private function, called only through `validate/2`) correctly detects violations at runtime/test time: it flattens all role_grants values, deduplicates, then checks each against `manifest.permissions`, returning `{:error, {:ungranted_permission_declared, bad_permission}}` on the first violation.

test/letflow/modules/catalog_test.exs exercises this rule correctly via an explicit inline manifest test case. The Fixture module (test/support/modules/fixture/fixture.ex) itself is valid: `permissions: [:FixtureRead]` and `role_grants: %{TASK_WORKER: [:FixtureRead]}` are consistent.

docs/migration/decisions/0039-platform-module-solution-layering.md (lines ~333-337) explicitly pre-announced this gap as non-blocking: 'module permissions are typed atom() at the Catalog boundary, which is a type-safety gap. When P1's code lands, REVIEWER should file it under docs/issues/ tagged type-safety. Candidate fix: a compile-time check that every role_grants atom is in permissions.'
reproduction.note: No mis-typed manifest currently exists in the codebase — the Fixture module is correctly authored. The defect is a missing constraint, not a live correctness failure. Reproduce by writing a module with role_grants referencing an undeclared permission: no compile error; only `Catalog.validate/1` catches it.

dialyzer_only_type_refinement.reasoning: Elixir/Erlang's type system (Dialyzer uses HM-style type inference over Erlang terms) cannot express a dependent/relational constraint between two sibling fields of the same map — specifically 'the atoms in the values of role_grants are a subset of the atoms in permissions'. A type alias `@type permission() :: atom()` would give a semantic label but provides no structural enforcement; Dialyzer would not flag a manifest where `role_grants` values contain atoms not in `permissions`. The constraint is set-membership across fields, not a type-level distinction.

defmanifest_macro.reasoning: A `defmanifest/1` macro defined in `Letflow.Modules.Module` (or a companion `Letflow.Modules.Module.DSL` module) can receive the manifest fields as a keyword list or quoted expression at compile time. Since real module manifests use compile-time literal atoms (the Fixture module and all anticipated real modules use static atom lists), the macro can evaluate the permissions list and role_grants map at macro-expansion time, then raise a `CompileError` if any role_grants value atom is absent from permissions. The macro still emits a `def manifest do ... end` function body, preserving the existing `@callback manifest/0` contract. `Catalog.validate/1` remains unchanged and continues to serve as second-line defense (for dynamically-constructed or test-inline manifests). This approach gives genuine compile-time feedback at module definition, not at test-run time.
defmanifest_macro.trade_off: Module authors must switch from `def manifest do ... end` to `defmanifest do ... end` (or an equivalent DSL call). For the current codebase this means updating exactly one file: test/support/modules/fixture/fixture.ex. Every future module gets the benefit automatically. If a module's manifest contains non-literal values (computed at runtime from config, for example), the compile-time check would require special handling (e.g., a runtime-only path that skips the compile-time guard but still defers to Catalog.validate/1).

before_compile_attribute_accumulator.reasoning: Modules could `use Letflow.Modules.Module`, declare `@permissions [...]` and `@role_grants %{...}` module attributes, and rely on a `@before_compile` hook to (a) validate role_grants ⊆ permissions and (b) generate the `manifest/0` function body. This removes the need for a separate `defmanifest` call but changes the interface from `@behaviour ... + def manifest` to `use ... + @attribute`. More moving parts, higher cognitive overhead for module authors, and a larger change to the existing Module behaviour interface. The @before_compile hook also runs after all module attributes are accumulated, which means errors surface slightly later in the compilation unit (at @before_compile time rather than at the point of the defmanifest call).

type_annotation_only_no_code_change.reasoning: Renaming types without any code validation mechanism (e.g., naming `@type declared_permission() :: atom()` and `@type granted_permission() :: atom()`) gives semantic clarity in @typedoc but provides no actual enforcement. Dialyzer still cannot see the cross-field constraint.

recommended_approach.rationale: Simplest mechanism that actually provides compile-time feedback. The macro evaluates at module-definition time, before the module is fully compiled, and raises a CompileError with a clear message (e.g., 'manifest role_grants atom :SomePermission not declared in permissions') if the constraint is violated. No process, no ETS, no runtime overhead. Existing Catalog.validate/1 runtime check and its test coverage are left entirely unchanged, as required by AC2.
affected_files: lib/letflow/modules/module.ex — add defmanifest/1 macro (or compile-time validation helper)
test/support/modules/fixture/fixture.ex — update manifest/0 definition to use defmanifest if macro approach adopted

acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC1_compile_time_check: defmanifest macro raises CompileError at module compilation if any role_grants value atom is absent from permissions
acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC2_runtime_validate_unchanged: Catalog.validate/1 and validate_granted_permissions_declared/1 are not modified; all six-rule checks continue to run when validate/1 is called

step_1_diagnosis.why_existing_tests_did_not_catch_this: The gap is a missing constraint at the type system / macro level, not a missing test case. The ExUnit test suite (CatalogTest) correctly tests validate_granted_permissions_declared/1 and would catch a bad manifest at test-run time. What is missing is enforcement at module compile time — before any test runs. No ExUnit test can enforce a compile-time contract.

This run is the first resolution attempt. No severity escalation: ISS-0790 is not a recurrence; the runtime validate/1 check has always been correct.
